newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds cheered by global placement.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds cheered by global placement.

text.p: Argentine bonds picked up Tuesday on the back of a successful launch of Argentina's 10-year global bond, dealers said.

Joint lead managers Goldman Sachs and Solomon Brothers announced Tuesday the bond had been fully placed and would be priced by Wednesday at between 445-450 basis points over the 10-year U.S. treasury note.
"This is more or less in line with expectations and it went down well in the market," said Oscar Barrera of Rabello traders.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.40 to 118.50 in early trading, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 3/4 to 84-5/8.
"The market remains basically firm, but the consensus now is that it has limited upside," said Barrera.
He noted the some of its recent strength had been sapped by news Argentina was not poised to launch a debt buyback scheme similar to Mexico's.
Traders said players would stay cautious in the run-up to Friday's U.S. jobs report, which could cause some mood swings in the New York treasuries market.
